scope: Three existing-function characterizations and two in-memory fault models of a proposed naive split; no real SQL migration or browser persistence exercised

checks.check: One existing sale command creates customer, sale and linked receipt
Customer email deduplication currently uses only this in-memory state
Existing transact restores memory when the single local save rejects
Modeled SQL-first split leaves committed catalog after local failure despite memory rollback
Modeled local-first split leaves sale referencing uncommitted customer after SQL rejection

conclusion: Existing memory rollback cannot coordinate separate durable stores; a recovery protocol and explicit restore scope are required before activation.
